title: Machine-Readable Dutch Law Schema v0.5.6
description: Article-based schema for machine-readable representation of Dutch laws and regulations

name.description: Name of the law/regulation (can be plain text or internal reference like '#wet_naam')

publication_date.description: Date when the law/regulation was officially published (publicatiedatum)

valid_from.description: Date when the law/regulation becomes effective (inwerkingtredingsdatum), or an internal reference starting with #

valid_to.description: Last calendar day on which the law/regulation is in force, inclusive (einddatum). Set ONLY when the law is terminated - it vervalt or wordt ingetrokken (a horizonbepaling/vervalbepaling, or repeal by another instrument); omit when a newer version of the same law simply takes over. A statutory 'vervalt met ingang van D' maps to valid_to = D minus one day. Must be a literal date (no internal references): the engine reads it as static version-selection metadata; end dates derived from another instrument or an executed article output are future work. See RFC-019.

url.description: Official URL to the law text

bwb_id.description: BWB identification number (for Dutch national laws)

celex_nummer.description: CELEX number (for EU regulations and directives)

unts_nummer.description: UN Treaty Series number (for international treaties)

waterschap_code.description: CBS water board code (for water board regulations)

organisation.description: Organization responsible (for implementation policies without official IDs)

legal_basis.description: Legal basis - articles from higher-level laws that authorize this regulation

law_id.description: Identifier of the law that provides authority

article.description: Article number that authorizes this regulation

description.description: Optional explanation of the legal relationship

preamble.description: Preamble/Aanhef section that appears before Article 1

text.description: Preamble text in markdown format, preserving original formatting from official publication

url.description: URL to the preamble in the official publication (if available)

number.description: Article number as it appears in the law

text.description: Article text in markdown format, preserving original formatting from official publication (numbered lists, links, paragraph structure)

placement.description: Where this article sits in the document: the containers that enclose it, each with its number and its opschrift. The opschrift is condensed legal classification written by the legislator, and it decides questions the article text alone cannot answer. Awb 3:9 only makes sense once you can see it sits in 'Afdeling 3.3 Advisering', because the adviseur definition of 3:5 lid 1 is scoped to that division. Absent for an article that no container encloses, which is normal in a short law.

number.description: Number of this container as the law gives it (e.g. '3.3')

references.description: Structured references to other laws/articles for runtime resolution

id.description: Reference ID used in markdown links (e.g., 'ref1')

procedure.description: AWB-defined procedure lifecycles for administrative decisions (RFC-008)

default.description: Whether this is the default procedure for its legal_character

requires.description: External inputs required to enter this stage

name.description: Field name (uppercase with underscores for constants)

type.description: Data type of the field value

type_spec.description: Additional type specifications for numeric and temporal values

unit.description: Unit of measurement for the value (RFC-023). A label, never a computational constraint: tagging a value never changes it. `ratio` (0-1) and `percentage` (0-100) are distinct labels; any division by 100 is an explicit value operation, never implied by the label.

precision.description: Number of decimal places for numeric values

temporal.description: Temporal metadata describing how values relate to time

type.description: Whether the value represents a period or point in time

period_type.description: Granularity of the period (for period type)

variableReference.description: Variable reference starting with $ (e.g., $standaardpremie, $referencedate.year). Supports dot notation for property access.

required.description: Whether this parameter must be provided (defaults to false)

source.description: Reference to where this input comes from

regulation.description: Name of external law/regulation. Omit for external data sources that must be resolved outside the YAML.

output.description: Output name to retrieve from the source

parameters.description: Parameters to pass when calling the source regulation (e.g., bsn: $bsn)

description.description: Human-readable description or legal reference for this data source

endpoint.description: Endpoint to call on the delegated regulation

arithmeticOperation.description: Arithmetic operations that compute numeric values

logicalOperation.description: Logical operations that combine boolean conditions

conditions.description: Conditions to combine - each item can be an operation, variable reference, or boolean literal

comparisonOperation.description: Comparison operations that compare values. Operands may be numbers or ISO 8601 dates (YYYY-MM-DD); when both operands are dates they are compared chronologically (RFC-021).

notOperation.description: Logical NOT - negates a boolean value

roundingOperation.description: Rounding operations (RFC-024). Round the single operand to `precision` decimal places, in the value's own unit (RFC-023). Rounding is never implicit - a law that rounds must say so here. ROUND is half-up (rekenkundig, the Hoge Raad default); CEIL rounds up (naar boven); FLOOR rounds down (naar beneden / afkapping).

precision.description: Number of decimal places to round to, in the value's own unit. 0 = whole units; 2 = two decimals; a negative value rounds to tens/hundreds (e.g. -2 rounds a eurocent value to whole euros).

ifOperation.description: Conditional operation with multiple cases evaluated in order

cases.description: List of when/then pairs evaluated in order

inOperation.description: Membership test - checks if subject is in a list

value.description: Single value or list reference to check against

ageOperation.description: Calculate age in complete years between two dates

reference_date.description: Reference date to calculate age at

dateAddOperation.description: Add years, months, weeks, and/or days to a date. Applied coarsest-to-finest: years → months → weeks → days. Month/year additions use the Dutch legal 'corresponding numbered day' rule: the day is clamped to the last day of the target month (e.g., Jan 31 + 1 month = Feb 28).

years.description: Number of years to add (clamped to last day of target month)

months.description: Number of months to add (clamped to last day of target month)

dateConstructOperation.description: Construct a date from year, month, day components

dayOfWeekOperation.description: Get the day of the week (0=Monday, 6=Sunday)

dateDiffOperation.description: Signed difference between two dates, expressed in a chosen unit. Positive when 'to' is on or after 'from'. Months and years count complete calendar units (RFC-021).

in.description: Unit the difference is expressed in: 'days', 'months', or 'years' (or a variable resolving to one of these)

operationType.description: Operation type identifier used in action definitions

operation.description: Executable operation that computes a value

output.description: Name of the output field this action computes

precision.description: Decimal places for an inline rounding operation (ROUND/CEIL/FLOOR; RFC-024), in the value's own unit. 0 = whole units; negative rounds to tens/hundreds.

resolve.description: Delegation resolution - resolve value from an implementing regulation

type.description: Regulatory layer to search for implementation

match.description: Matching criteria for selecting the right implementation

explanation.description: Dutch explanation of how this element relates to the law text

endpoint.description: Named endpoint for this article, making it callable from other regulations

competent_authority.description: Bevoegd gezag - authority whose execution produces binding decisions

type.description: INSTANCE = specific organization (default), CATEGORY = must be resolved per context

requires.description: Dependencies on other articles, regelingen, or external sources

open_terms.description: Abstract values that this article leaves open and that an implementing regulation or implementing policy fills at a lower level. Any regulatory layer can declare open_terms; a law typically has required: true (no default), lower layers often provide defaults that can be refined further down. This is the single place for an open norm, whether the article names who fills it ('bij ministeriele regeling') or leaves that open ('redelijkerwijs'); in the second case delegated_to and delegation_type are simply absent and any competent authority may fill it through implementing policy. Whether the filling regulation is currently in the corpus is a state of the corpus and not a property of the law, so it is not recorded here.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this term represents

type.description: Data type of the expected value

required.description: Whether an implementation is mandatory (true) or optional with possible default (false)

delegated_to.description: Who the article authorises to fill this term (e.g. 'Onze Minister', 'gemeenteraad'). Absent when the article names nobody, which leaves the term to whichever authority is competent in the individual case.

delegation_type.description: The regulatory layer the article requires of the implementation (e.g. 'MINISTERIELE_REGELING'). An implementation at another layer does not fill this term.

legal_basis.description: Legal basis text (e.g., 'artikel 4 Wet op de zorgtoeslag')

default.description: Default execution logic when no implementing regulation is found. Makes the article executable standalone while still allowing refinement via implements.

implements.description: Declares that this article fills open terms from a higher-level law. Maps to the 'Gelet op' clause in Dutch legislation. One article can implement multiple open terms from different laws.

law.description: The $id of the higher-level law being implemented (e.g., 'wet_op_de_zorgtoeslag')

article.description: Article number in the higher law that declares the open_term (e.g., '4')

gelet_op.description: Legal reference text (e.g., 'Gelet op artikel 4 van de Wet op de zorgtoeslag')

definitions.description: Definitions and constants. Each entry is either a bare value (`naam: 123`) or the optionally-structured form carrying a `type` and `type_spec` so the constant can declare its quantity-kind (RFC-023): `naam: {value: 123, type: amount, type_spec: {unit: eurocent}}`.

procedure_id.description: Selects a specific AWB procedure variant. When absent, the default procedure for the legal_character is used.

actions.description: Actions that compute outputs or make decisions

hooks.description: Hook declarations: this article fires when matching lifecycle events occur (RFC-007)

hook_point.description: When in the lifecycle this hook fires

legal_character.description: Match articles that produce this legal character

decision_type.description: Optionally narrow to a specific decision type

stage.description: Lifecycle stage at which this hook fires (e.g., BESLUIT, BEKENDMAKING). Defaults to BESLUIT.

overrides.description: Override declarations: this article replaces another article's output (RFC-007, lex specialis)

law.description: The $id of the law being overridden

voids.description: The overridden output does not arise at all, rather than being replaced by another value. "Bestaat geen aanspraak" is not an entitlement of zero: with an entitlement of zero there is a decision carrying legal remedies and a ground for recovery, and with no entitlement there is neither. An engine reads this flag and nothing else; it needs no knowledge of administrative law to act on it.

legal_text_excerpt.description: The words of this article that establish the override, quoted verbatim, as `markings` already do. A closed vocabulary was considered and rejected: it would make the agent translate the statute into a category, which is the interpretive step this format exists to avoid. A quotation only has to be copied, and a check can hold it against the article's own text.

markings.description: Constructs in this article that the format itself cannot express. A marking is a flag on an article that is otherwise worked out: it names the one thing that does not fit and leaves everything that does fit standing. A marking that empties an article is a defect, not a translation. Keep it strictly apart from open_terms, which say the opposite: the language can express this fine, the content is filled elsewhere. Replaces untranslatables and norm_gaps from earlier schema versions.

about.description: The construct that cannot be expressed, in the words the article uses (e.g. 'het kalenderjaar waarop de tegemoetkoming betrekking heeft')

resolution.description: What has to change before this article can be translated in full. engine: the operation does not exist and must be built (statutory rounding, extracting the year from a date). model: the operation set is not the problem; the format has no shape for this construct (quantification over persons, a rule about a set rather than a value, a legal fiction). Nothing else belongs here: a norm whose content is filled by another regulation is an open_term, and a value produced by another law is an input with a source.

resolved_by.description: The change that would resolve it, named concretely enough to become work (e.g. 'Een YEAR-bewerking die het jaardeel van een datum oplevert'). Grouping markings by this field is how the backlog of missing operations is read off the corpus.

target.description: The values in this article that cannot be produced because of this marking: outputs, inputs or parameters by name. An empty list is a statement and not an omission: it says the article stays executable and only its explanation is incomplete. Every name listed here must be absent from the article's actions; computing a value you declared blocked is a contradiction.

legal_text_excerpt.description: The words from this article's own legal text that the marking hangs on. Required: a marking that cannot quote the text it is about is about something else.

accepted.description: Whether a human has reviewed and acknowledged this gap. Accepted markings are allowed in error mode.

declares.description: Document properties this article establishes. A citation title, a commencement date or a scope in time is not a calculation, and it is not nothing either: it fixes a value the rest of the corpus and every trace depend on. Article 51 of the Awir says what that law is called, and a trace that names the law is quoting that article. Recording it here makes the article accounted for and lets a check hold the document header against the provision that decides it.

property.description: The top-level document property this article fixes.

value.description: The value the article gives it, verbatim from the text.

applies_from.description: Where the article limits the property in time beyond the value itself, e.g. Awir article 50, which commences on 1 September 2005 but applies to berekeningsjaren from 1 January 2006.
